These mechanisms together aim to maintain transfer integrity and concurrency control, though exact once-only execution under all failure conditions is not independently verified.

cases.question: How do BlockScan and Cleanup differ?
cases.answer: BlockScan and Approval Cleanup differ primarily in their purpose and functionality within the blockchain ecosystem. BlockScan is a blockchain explorer for the Ethereum Sepolia test network, allowing users to inspect blocks, transactions, wallet addresses, account activity, and NFT metadata. It features live data feeds, global search distinguishing block numbers, transactions, and addresses, and includes a persistent watchlist and credential handling to protect API keys. In contrast, Approval Cleanup is an ERC-20 wallet-permission manager that helps users review and manage token allowances granted to other addresses or contracts. It scans recent Approval events to identify current token-spender permissions, highlighting risky or unlimited approvals, and allows users to update or revoke these permissions through their connected wallets. While BlockScan focuses on data exploration and monitoring, Approval Cleanup centers on permission management and security for token spending.

# BlockScan — Sepolia blockchain explorer

**Type:** Independent frontend project  
**Repository:** https://github.com/faelic/sepolia-blockexplorer  
**Application:** https://blockscan-seven.vercel.app/  
**Stack:** React, JavaScript, React Router, React Testing Library, Alchemy SDK/RPC, Vercel.

## Overview

BlockScan is a blockchain explorer for Ethereum Sepolia. It lets users inspect blocks, transactions, wallet addresses, account activity, and NFT metadata.

## Search and live-data implementation

Favour built a global search feature that distinguishes block numbers, transaction hashes, and wallet addresses and opens the appropriate result. The live-block feed checks for new data while preventing overlapping requests and duplicate results. It preserves the existing results if a refresh fails and avoids unnecessary polling when the page is not visible.

BlockScan's live-block feed also avoids updates that overwrite valid information.

## Navigation, watchlist, and credential handling

For BlockScan, Favour also built a persistent watchlist, keyboard-accessible search, route-level code splitting, and Vercel API proxies that keep Alchemy credentials out of the browser bundle.

The credentials described here are Alchemy provider API credentials, not
database credentials. This documents a credential-exposure control, not
proof that the application prevents every form of unauthorized access.

# Approval Cleanup — ERC-20 wallet-permission manager

**Type:** Independent blockchain application  
**Also known as:** Cleanup; Allowance Cleanup.  
**Repository:** https://github.com/faelic/approval-cleanup  
**Application:** https://approval-cleanup-brt3.vercel.app/  
**Stack:** Next.js, React, TypeScript, wagmi, viem, Hardhat, OpenZeppelin.

## Overview and contribution

Approval Cleanup helps wallet owners review ERC-20 token allowances granted to other addresses or contracts. Favour built the interface for scanning recent Approval events, identifying the latest observed token-and-spender allowances, and calling attention to permissions that deserve a closer look, including unlimited and older approvals.

Approval Cleanup scans a recent block window and cannot guarantee a complete history of every approval a wallet has ever granted.

## Log processing and wallet actions

Approval Cleanup retrieves logs in batches that work within RPC provider limits, then separates normalization and risk checks from the interface. Users can review an allowance and initiate an update or revocation through their connected wallet.

Approval Cleanup's scan covers a recent block window; provider constraints and non-standard tokens can affect the results.

## Coverage limitations

Because Approval Cleanup's scan covers a recent block window, it cannot guarantee a complete history of every approval a wallet has ever granted. Non-standard tokens and provider constraints can also affect what the application finds.

Section: Portfolio RAG Assistant — Portfolio questions and grounded answers > Python implementation and retrieval

## Python implementation and retrieval  
The Portfolio RAG Assistant uses Python, LangChain, OpenAI embeddings and chat models, Chroma, and Gradio. Its ingestion pipeline loads curated Markdown, extracts YAML metadata separately from searchable text, preserves document identity and section metadata, and creates deterministic heading-aware chunks. The local synchronization workflow upserts current chunks before deleting obsolete records.  
The answering pipeline performs semantic retrieval and constructs a grounded answer from the retrieved passages. For conversation follow-ups, it rewrites the question into a standalone retrieval query while preserving the original question for answering. The documented configuration uses text-embedding-3-large for embeddings and gpt-4.1-mini for answering.

Favour is the sole frontend engineer on the product. He builds and maintains the public-facing pages and authenticated administration tools using React and TypeScript. His work includes policy search and detail views, public-official directories, AI-assisted question interfaces, comments and administrative replies, moderation, content editing, and subscriber management.  
His responsibility at Policy.ng is the frontend, including the integration of its AI-assisted question interface. The product's backend and underlying AI services are separate from that frontend responsibility.
